paragraph: PROPHET OF THE LORD IN THE DAYS OF AHAB, THE ONE AHAB SAID HE HATED · TWO KINGDOMS

blocks.text: PROPHET OF THE LORD IN THE DAYS OF AHAB, THE ONE AHAB SAID HE HATED · TWO KINGDOMS
Micaiah. One man against four hundred: “what the LORD saith unto me, that will I speak.”
He bound himself by oath, before he reached the king: “what the LORD saith unto me, that will I speak.”
He bound himself by oath, before he reached the king: “what the LORD saith unto me, that will I speak.” 1 Kings 22:14
His first answer repeated the four hundred: “Go, and prosper”. Only when the king adjured him to tell “nothing but that which is true” did he tell what he had seen. 1 Kings 22:15–16
He spoke in visions: “I saw all Israel scattered upon the hills”, and “I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him”. 1 Kings 22:17 1 Kings 22:19

From the textKings and Chronicles side by side. Ahab's complaint: “he doth not prophesy good concerning me, but evil” (Kings), “he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil” (Chronicles). Micaiah's oath: “what the LORD saith unto me” (Kings), “even what my God saith” (Chronicles). His first answer in Chronicles: “Go ye up, and prosper, and they shall be delivered into your hand”. The spirit offers to “persuade” Ahab in Kings and to “entice” him in Chronicles; Kings has “all these thy prophets”, Chronicles “these thy prophets”. His last word is “If thou return at all in peace” in Kings; Chronicles words the condition with a different adverb. Chronicles has no dogs at the pool of Samaria. 1 Kings 22:8 1 Kings 22:14–15 1 Kings 22:20–23 1 Kings 22:28 1 Kings 22:38 2 Chronicles 18:7 +4 more
“If thou return at all in peace, the LORD hath not spoken by me.”
“Is there not here a prophet of the LORD besides, that we might enquire of him?”
The word in its main themes
“As the LORD liveth, what the LORD saith unto me, that will I speak.”
“I saw all Israel scattered upon the hills, as sheep that have not a shepherd: and the LORD said, These have no master: let them return every man to his house in peace.”
A lying spirit in the prophets' mouths
“Now therefore, behold, the LORD hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and the LORD hath spoken evil concerning thee.”
To whom the word was spoken
“As the LORD liveth, what the LORD saith unto me, that will I speak.”
“Hear thou therefore the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.”
“Behold, thou shalt see in that day, when thou shalt go into an inner chamber to hide thyself.”
“Hearken, O people, every one of you.”
Who stood with him, and against him

Ahab ordered: “Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I come in peace.” Micaiah's last recorded words are his answer. 1 Kings 22:26–28

Ahab went up to Ramoth-gilead disguised; an arrow drawn “at a venture” struck him between the joints of the harness, and he “died at even”. A cry went through the host, “Every man to his city, and every man to his own country.” 1 Kings 22:29–37
Chronicles tells the same and ends “about the time of the sun going down he died”. 2 Chronicles 18:28–34
From the textScripture does not say what became of Micaiah after he was led away. 1 Kings 22:26–28
Keil calls the identification “mere conjecture”, while inferring from “carry him back” (22:26) that Ahab had already imprisoned Micaiah for an unwelcome prophecy. 1 Kings 22:8 1 Kings 22:26 [1]
Scripture records no call for Micaiah and no other prophecy than this one scene.
Kings and Chronicles do not say whether Micaiah was released, or how his story ended.
Scripture does not say why Ahab had to “carry him back” to Amon (1 Kings 22:26), or for what earlier word.
